discussion_comments.comment_body:
This suppress is hiding something users will hit. When the outer ALPN list isn't a subset of the inner one and the server rejects ECH, the client doesn't get SSLECHRejectedError. It gets a plain SSLError (BAD_EXTENSION), with no retry_config, and get_ech_status() reports ECH_STATUS_FAILED. I tried three combinations against OpenSSL 4.0 with a stale config:
 
| inner        | outer    | client result                             |
|--------------|----------|-------------------------------------------|
| h2           | unset    | SSLECHRejectedError, retry config present |
| h2, http/1.1 | http/1.1 | SSLECHRejectedError, retry config present |
| h2           | http/1.1 | SSLError: BAD_EXTENSION, no retry config  |

This breaks the recovery flow in [RFC 9849 6.1.6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9849/#name-handshaking-with-clienthello) for anyone using set_outer_alpn_protocols() the way [10.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9849/#name-outer-clienthello) contemplates (a different, non-sensitive list in the outer hello).

I think this is an OpenSSL bug - cc: @sftcd . In ssl/statem/extensions_clnt.c (openssl-4.0), tls_parse_stoc_alpn() validates the server's selection against s->ext.alpn (the inner list) unconditionally and raises SSL_R_BAD_EXTENSION. tls_construct_ctos_alpn() sent s->ext.ech.alpn_outer in the outer hello, and after rejection that is the list the server chose from. The SNI parser in the same file already handles this case ("if we tried ECH and failed, the outer is what's expected"); ALPN doesn't. Because the handshake dies there, it never reaches the ech_required abort in statem_clnt.c that sets retry_configs_ok, which is why no retry config is available. OpenSSL's own tests only use disjoint inner/outer ALPN on the success path.  Worth raising upstream.  _[This was Claude Fable's finding by analyzing the behavior, RFC, and code -gps]_

What to do? For now, assuming that is an upstream issue, lets document the constraint on set_outer_alpn_protocols(). Should this test assert the actual exception rather than suppress it, so we notice when the behavior changes or is that going to turn into a change-detector based on the version/behavior of OpenSSL linked against?

We _could_ just assert the server-side ALPN as now and add a comment linking the upstream issue, so the suppress is explained perhaps.
